svg.title: Which of the following are appropriate nursing actions for a client with a chest tube? Select all that apply.
svg.desc: Keeping the unit below chest level uses gravity to drain and prevents backflow; coiling tubing, taping connections, and monitoring the site are all standard. Stripping or milking is never routine — it generates extreme negative pressure that can damage lung tissue.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Chest Tube Care
Read the situation
Which of the following are appropriate
nursing actions for a client with a chest
tube? Select all that apply.
What fits here
Keep the drainage system below the level
of the client's chest · Coil the tubing
flat on the bed to prevent dependent loops
· Monitor the insertion site for redness
and drainage · Tape all…
Why it fits
Keeping the unit below chest level uses
gravity to drain and prevents backflow;
coiling tubing, taping connections, and
monitoring the site are all standard.
Stripping or milking is never routine — it
generates extreme negative pressure that
can damage lung tissue.
